title: The point-ideal Picard class represents the explicit divisor module
statement: Let k be algebraically closed and C a smooth connected curve over k, with its structure morphism smooth of relative dimension one. For every (possibly negative) divisor D, the chosen representative of the Picard class Divisor.toPic k C D is isomorphic to the valuation-bounded module O_C(D) of [def-sc-divisor].

source.place: Proof, homomorphism step (step 3 in the DAG), combined with lem-pc-divisor-line-bundle-agrees-sc; Stacks Divisors 02SL

proof.text: Extract the invertibility of O(D) from lem-sc-divisor-module-local: lem-sc-smooth-connected-curve-local-rings supplies a closed point and a DVR stalk. Take a principal generator of its maximal ideal using Ideal.span_singleton_generator and project the invertibility clause of Divisor.module_local. This argument works for every divisor.

Write D=A-B using Divisor.mapRange_toNat_sub, with A and B the natural-number-valued positive and negative parts cast to integer divisors. For every effective E, rewrite the product in divisorLineBundle_agrees_sc by Finsupp.prod_mapRange_index and Nat.toNat_natCast. It identifies O(E) with the dual of Divisor.idealSheaf E. Pic.ofIsInvertible_eq_of_iso and Pic.ofIsInvertible_dual give the inverse ideal class.

Apply lem-sc-divisor-module-tensor-add to D and B. Since D+B=A, Pic.ofIsInvertible_tensorObj gives [O(D)] [O(B)]=[O(A)]. Divisor.toMul_toPic_mapRange_sub and the effective comparisons also give (Divisor.toPic k C D).toMul [O(B)]=[O(A)]. Cancel [O(B)] in Pic(C), then use Pic.eq_ofIsInvertible_iff to obtain the asserted isomorphism of representatives. No separate comparison for O(0) or inverse-module isomorphism is needed.

proof_origin.place: Proof, homomorphism step: effective positive/negative parts and tensor cancellation; formalized by P2.
